name: Yugh (Retired)
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: yugh1240 is a retired Glottolog bookkeeping code for Yugh (Yeniseian; current code yugh1239), not in the catalog. this search of works with stress in the title's single title item, Lehfeldt 2001 'Einführung in die morphologische Konzeption der slavischen Akzentologie', is a Slavic/Lithuanian accentology monograph; Glottolog's own record (ref 20942, saved) says its link to 'Yugh (Retired) [yuu]' is a computerized assignment from the keyword 'akzentologie'. Irrelevant, priority none, not downloaded (print-only Sagner book, no DOI). The best first-hand stress statement for Yugh remains Werner 1997 (Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки, p. 189 §2.1.2), already held by the project from an earlier reading and re-read here: a four-tone language where stress is essentially the syllable that retains its tone, plus two short-syllable accent types with a pitch rise on the first vs. last/penultimate syllable, only the first resembling dynamic word stress. direct download still worked for the Glottolog record. Directory: ( updated with the new line).

new_statements.quote: 2.1.2. В Ю.я. обнаружено четыре слоговых тона [...] Наиболее четко тоны реализуются в изолированных односложных словах; в многосложных словах они могут сохраняться лишь в ударных слогах. В последнем случае ударение является по существу мерой полноты реализации тона. Иное положение наблюдается при реализации двух особых краткосложных акцентных типов: при одном из них наблюдается повышение основного тона голоса на первом (ударном) слоге, при другом — на последнем или предпоследнем (ударном) слоге при одинаковой интенсивности во всех слогах: dʌnɯŋ ‘ножи’, kanča ‘курительная трубка’. Первый тип производит впечатление динамического словесного ударения.
new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Four syllabic tones have been found in Yugh [...] The tones are realized most clearly in isolated monosyllabic words; in polysyllabic words they can be preserved only in stressed syllables. In the latter case stress is essentially a measure of the completeness of realization of the tone. A different situation is observed in the realization of two special short-syllable accent types: in one of them a rise of the fundamental frequency is observed on the first (stressed) syllable, in the other on the last or penultimate (stressed) syllable, with equal intensity in all syllables: dʌnɯŋ 'knives', kanča 'smoking pipe'. The first type gives the impression of dynamic word stress.
new_statements.citation: Вернер Г. К. [Heinrich Werner]. 1997. Югский язык. In: А. П. Володин и др. (ред.), Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки. Москва: Индрик, с. 187–195.
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the copies we hold under The Rosetta Project scan archive.org item rosettaproject_yuu_phon-1, 3 pages, 'Yugh Phonology', pp.188-189 of Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки 1997) has page 189 as p.2; I viewed the 300-dpi render and the passage crop (..) directly, plus the tesseract-rus text. Page header reads 'Г. К. Вернер. Югский язык 189'. §2.1.2 is exactly as quoted: the four-tone feature table (высокий регистр / фарингализация / циркумфлексный контур / отрывистость), then 'Наиболее четко тоны реализуются в изолированных односложных словах; в многосложных словах они могут сохраняться лишь в ударных слогах. В последнем случае ударение является по существу мерой полноты реализации тона.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Yugh is described as a tone (syllable-accent) language with four phonemic syllabic tones, fully realized on monosyllables; in polysyllabic words the tone survives only on the stressed syllable, and 'stress' is defined as the degree to which the tone is realized. Position of the stressed/tone-bearing syllable is not given as a fixed rule: Werner describes two accent types for words of short syllables, one with the pitch peak on the first syllable (sounding like dynamic initial stress) and one with the peak on the final or penultimate syllable. Function morphemes/semi-suffixes are normally unstressed and reduced (§2.2.2), and unstressed syllables have a reduced 7-vowel inventory (§2.1.3). The ИЯз РАН portal (second-hand) adds that tones occur only on the first syllable of the root morpheme.
new_statements.exceptions: Two 'special short-syllable accent types' (initial-peak vs. final/penultimate-peak, e.g. dʌnɯŋ 'knives' vs. kanča 'pipe'); function morphemes and semi-suffixes (e.g. -d'eŋ 'people') usually unstressed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; tones described on isolated (citation-form) monosyllables; stress discussed for polysyllabic words. No explicit default stress position; the parallel Ket chapter by the same author (same volume p.179) calls Ket word stress 'free', but the Yugh chapter does not repeat this.
new_statements.identity_note: yugh1240 is a retired Glottolog bookkeeping code; the source describes Yugh = Sym Ket (сымский диалект кетского / Sym-Ketisch), i.e. the live languoid yugh1239 (ISO 639-3 yug; the Rosetta/older ISO code was yuu). Werner's data are from the last speakers at Ворогово and Ярцево (1960s–70s); the language is extinct.

new_statements.quote: В многосложных словах [тоны] могут сохраняться лишь в ударных слогах. В последнем случае ударение является по существу мерой полноты реализации тона. Иное положение наблюдается при реализации двух особых краткосложных акцентных типов: при одном из них наблюдается повышение основного тона голоса на первом (ударном) слоге, при другом — на последнем или предпоследнем (ударном) слоге при одинаковой интенсивности во всех слогах: dʌnyŋ ‘ножи’, kanča ‘курительная трубка’. Первый тип производит впечатление динамического словесного ударения.
new_statements.translation: In polysyllabic words [the tones] can be preserved only in stressed syllables. In that case stress is essentially a measure of the completeness of the tone's realization. A different situation is observed in the realization of two special short-syllable accent types: in one of them a rise of the fundamental frequency of the voice is observed on the first (stressed) syllable, in the other on the last or penultimate (stressed) syllable, with equal intensity in all syllables: dʌnyŋ 'knives', kanča 'smoking pipe'. The first type gives the impression of dynamic word stress.
new_statements.citation: Вернер, Г. К. [Werner, Heinrich]. 1997. Югский язык. In А. П. Володин et al. (eds.), Языки мира: Палеоазиатские языки, 187–195. Москва: Индрик. (Rosetta Project scan, archive.org rosettaproject_yuu_phon-1)
new_statements.locator: p. 189, §2.1.2 (phonology: syllable tones), paragraph after the four-tone feature table
new_statements.reading: Yugh is described as a four-tone (syllable-tone) language in which 'stress' is not an independent, positionally fixed parameter: the stressed syllable of a polysyllable is the one that keeps its tone, so stress is a by-product of tone realization. Only in two minor short-syllable accent types does a pitch rise mark a stressed syllable, on the first syllable in one type and on the final or penultimate in the other, with no intensity difference; only the first of these resembles dynamic word stress. Word-stress placement is therefore lexically variable / tone-driven, not predictable from edge or weight. This is the same first-hand statement recorded in the earlier reading on this directory (see there); the present search's only title item (Lehfeldt 2001) adds nothing. §2.2.2 (p. 190) adds that function morphemes are mostly unstressed.
